scope: Complete finite graph audit of necessary support conditions. Remaining graphs are not asserted to admit simultaneous integer charts, atlases, or fibrations.
canonical_rule: Lexicographically smallest sorted edge tuple on active labels 0,...,n-1.

research_priorities.next: Extend the full one-high-leaf normal form and marked coefficient transfer to its three-high or four-high neighbor. The existing leaf-to-degree-two transfer theorem does not apply directly. Retain all low-low freedoms and both branches at remaining degree-two cores.
Compare all positive and negative two-high branches using low-edge nodes. G5_11 has common-low triples (13;4),(24;3); G5_13 has none, so no blanket ordinary reverse bound is imposed.
Use three-high matching only at degree-three cores, fixed-low quadratic reconstruction, and dense prime-support lifting. The degree-two core in G5_15 may be on the negative branch.

limitations: The graph audit applies proved arithmetic obstructions; enumeration is not a replacement for those proofs.
New removals concern equality of the whole high-support graph. The remaining G5_15, G5_16, G5_17 contain K4 subgraphs and are not removed for that reason.
Every remaining degree-two vertex lies on a high triangle; this does not prove that its negative local branch can be globally realized.
Local matrix families or surviving support graphs are not simultaneous five-core charts or geometric atlases.
The scope is the specified standard quintic model, not all surfaces of general type or all Lagrangian torus fibrations.
